## Outcome

The selected C1–C4 solved pressures, densities, compositions and phase fractions meet the **cross-library value** targets. FeOs acetone saturation does not: the relative pressure difference is $1.21\times10^{-7}$ and vapor-density difference $1.22\times10^{-7}$ against $10^{-8}$. The motivating NaCl anchors are reproduced. Their gap is explained by controlled, ordered changes in screening diameter, electrostatic constants, water–chloride interaction and ionic reference, not by diameter alone.

This is not universal strict equation agreement. Raw common-state differences and computed source-error-adjusted differences remain separate. Dispersion coefficient precision, dipole conversion and the Clapeyron DH approximation explain important differences. Dense-liquid $\ln\phi$ still misses its absolute target after those corrections. C4 has an additional Clapeyron association derivative remainder. **The corrected Engine closes all 12 primary NaCl states and all 14 reference-ladder states below the unchanged $10^{-10}$ relative pressure target:** their maxima are $6.96\times10^{-11}$ and $8.46\times10^{-11}$. The original Engine maximum $3.88\times10^{-10}$ remains under its original wheel identity. Clapeyron C4 pressure/chemical closure still reaches about $2.88\times10^{-9}$. A passing comparison between libraries does not override these failed checks.

The evidence is **numerical verification**, not experimental validation, parameter adoption, a global-stability result or a portable speed ranking. The owner-approved revision changes native density endpoint publication and anchor return, keeping all numerical-policy values and comparison targets. The first benchmark delivery received independent review; delivered review of this density correction remains open. These results have not been promoted for manuscript use.

## Original agreement on the declared cases

All quantities use SI pressure in Pa and molar density in mol/m³. $a^r=A^r/(nRT)$, $Z$, $\ln\phi_i$, molality-scale $\gamma_\pm$, practical $\Phi$, mole fractions and mole phase fractions are dimensionless. Relative differences use Engine as denominator; composition and logarithmic comparisons use absolute differences. Maxima below exclude intentionally unmatched NaCl convention rows.

| Case and conditions | FeOs versus Engine | Clapeyron versus Engine | Target/disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 propane; 200, 250, 300, 350 K | max relative P $5.68\times10^{-10}$; density $5.74\times10^{-10}$ | P/density at most $4.83\times10^{-15}$ relative | Solved-value $10^{-8}$ met |
| C2 ethanol/butane; 373.15 K; liquid ethanol x=0.2, 0.5, 0.8 | P $1.65\times10^{-10}$; density $2.26\times10^{-10}$ relative; vapor x $1.94\times10^{-11}$ absolute | P/density at most $3.42\times10^{-13}$ relative | Solved-value targets met |
| C3 NaCl; 298.15 K, 1 bar; 0.01–4 mol/kg; matched 0.88σ | density $7.99\times10^{-11}$ relative; $|\Delta\ln\gamma|=1.18\times10^{-6}$; $|\Delta\Phi|=2.48\times10^{-8}$ | density $5.05\times10^{-11}$; $|\Delta\ln\gamma|=1.18\times10^{-6}$; $|\Delta\Phi|=2.27\times10^{-8}$ | C3 coefficient target $10^{-5}$ met |
| C3 unchanged σ screening | Not a matching FeOs option | density $1.03\times10^{-10}$ relative; $|\Delta\ln\gamma|=1.18\times10^{-6}$; $|\Delta\Phi|=4.62\times10^{-8}$ | Held screening selection preserved |
| C4 water/pentanol; 298.15/323.15 K, 101300 Pa | density $7.77\times10^{-11}$ relative; x $7.40\times10^{-11}$; water-rich mole fraction $9.40\times10^{-11}$ absolute | density at most $5.03\times10^{-12}$ relative; x at most $4.26\times10^{-12}$; fraction $5.55\times10^{-12}$ absolute | Nontrivial split; value targets met, closure misses below |
| C5 acetone; 300 K | raw P/vapor density $1.2074\times10^{-7}$/$1.2187\times10^{-7}$ relative; matched dipole P/vapor density $1.1988\times10^{-7}$/$1.2100\times10^{-7}$ | raw P $8.62\times10^{-10}$; matched dipole P $3.29\times10^{-15}$ | FeOs pressure/vapor-density targets missed |
| C1/C2 exact P gradients | max relative difference $1.92\times10^{-10}$ / $2.24\times10^{-10}$ | Not selected under adopted D6 | Every selected component meets mixed rule |

The gradient rule is $|g_L-g_E|\le10^{-6}\max(|g_L|,|g_E|)+10^{-8}$. C1 coordinates are $(m,\sigma,\epsilon/k)$ with units Pa, Pa/Å, Pa/K. C2 coordinates are $(k,\epsilon^{AB}/k,\kappa^{AB})$ with units Pa, Pa/K, Pa; one self-edge coordinate changes both directional association edges. These are physical pressure derivatives, not weighted fit-residual gradients. No Clapeyron gradient-capability conclusion follows from D6.

[values.csv](results/values.csv) owns exact values, signed differences, units and target outcomes. [states.csv](inputs/states.csv) owns the exact common-state inputs. Each comparator is evaluated at the Engine solved $(T,\rho_m,x)$ for common-state rows, not at its own equilibrium density.

† Original Engine timing returns were not retained and remain unqualified. The costs are preserved historical measurements; no future snapshot qualifies those missing returns.

The Engine T1 state path returns its normal derivatives and contributions. FeOs State construction plus requested properties and Clapeyron scalar/chemical-potential calls do different additional work. Engine T2 uses the general equilibrium driver. Engine T3 includes `predict` plus `differentiate`; the latter performs another prediction. FeOs's native AD property interface includes its internal solve; C2 also includes a native bubble solve to obtain the AD pressure guess. Models are constructed outside warm timing, but automatic solve initialization and returned-value extraction are inside.

Engine C3 reused-reference timing excludes only the explicitly preconstructed reference. Its fresh-reference row includes reference construction. FeOs C3 times native solution/reference states, serialization, the compiled Julia contraction and transport. Clapeyron C3 times **both** native activity/osmotic helpers, each of which repeats solution/reference solves; it is not a cached-reference workload.

Three fresh-process median ranges show substantial case-dependent scatter: Engine C2 21.28–26.92 ms; FeOs C4 at 298.15 K 30.39–45.00 ms; Clapeyron C4 at 298.15 K 0.879–0.985 ms. The 124.8 ms Clapeyron warm outlier is retained, not trimmed. The 642 retained comparator fields reproduce the corresponding implementation's qualification baseline (306 FeOs, 336 Clapeyron). The original Engine timing files contain no returned numerical records, so Engine timed outputs remain unqualified. Comparator records are first-call outputs collected outside warm timing, not independent numerical snapshots of all 25 warm samples.

The host is an AMD Ryzen 5 5500, six cores/twelve logical CPUs, CPU 0 affinity, qualification-time performance governor snapshot, `nice -n 10`, and one thread in every pool. The governor was not logged separately in the timing processes; the qualification snapshot cannot establish its value throughout those measurements. Normal optimized Julia has `compile_enabled=1`, optimization level 2. Measured cold block sums (imports, model construction and first calls) are 604–696 s per Julia process, 0.230–0.334 s Engine and 0.603–0.709 s FeOs. These exclude unmeasured process-launch work and are not warm speed estimates. Total measured warm work including warmups is 22.955 s, below 1200 s; the maximum measured sample is 0.229 s, below the 180 s case limit.

The original 300 s Julia cold cap was exhausted during inference/compilation. The lead authorized 1800 s and retired the global flock. Normal optimized qualification and all three timing repetitions then completed. `--compile=min` probes are not used as benchmark evidence. [timings.csv](results/timings.csv), [timing-statistics.csv](results/timing-statistics.csv), [budgets.csv](results/budgets.csv) and [original qualification checks](results/timed-output-checks-original.csv) retain the measurements and checks.

## Model basis and input mappings

[full-eos](../../engine/docs/science/full-eos.md) §§2, 4–6, 8, 10–11 owns the equations and quantity bases. [cases.json](inputs/cases.json) freezes cited component records, explicit zero/nonzero interactions, site/component order, constants, solver selections and gradient identities. C1 reuses GS2001 propane; C2/C4 reuse GS2002 neutral/2B data and cited interactions; C3 reuses the complete Held strategy-2 packet; C5 reuses GV2006 acetone. The existing [polar study](../2026-polar-dipole/README.md) is independent dipole-term evidence on its retained rows only; it is not rerun here.

C3 uses temperature-dependent Held water σ, ion segment counts of one, ion **packing** diameters 0.88σ, excluded same-sign dispersion, all packet unlike interactions, constant solvent-only εr=78.09 and Born off. Screening diameter is a separate input: unchanged σ versus an analysis-local 0.88σ variant. Neither variant replaces the adopted Held packet. FeOs revised ePC-SAFT exposes the latter screening convention only.

Each library's electrostatic constants are retained. Compensated permittivity

$$
\epsilon_{r,L}=78.09\left(\frac{e_L}{e_E}\right)^2
\frac{\epsilon_{0,E}}{\epsilon_{0,L}}\frac{k_{B,E}}{k_{B,L}}
$$

preserves the same Bjerrum factor. Literal εr=78.09 rows remain convention diagnostics. This is a numerical input mapping, not a new measured dielectric constant. The locked FeOs quantity constants $N_A,k_B,R$ agree with the Engine selection. Its vacuum permittivity is older; Clapeyron also uses an older charge constant. Bjerrum lengths, screening factors and evaluated water diameters are retained rather than inferred from names.

### Association and C4 feed

Every associating molecule has one donor A and one acceptor B; only A–B/B–A edges exist. Unlike edges use arithmetic association energy and

$$
\kappa^{AB}_{ij}=\sqrt{\kappa^{AB}_{ii}\kappa^{AB}_{jj}}
\left[\frac{\sqrt{\sigma_i\sigma_j}}{(\sigma_i+\sigma_j)/2}\right]^3.
$$

Engine explicit derived edges, FeOs's native geometric volume factor and Clapeyron explicit dimensionless `bondvol` with `combining=:nocombining` therefore enter the same source strength. Clapeyron's m³ docstring is not the parameter basis used here. The independently returned cross-volume check tests parameter construction, not a native Δ or site-solver residual.

At the required fixed falsifier, $\rho_m=10000$ mol/m³ and $x=(0.5,0.5)$, native association energies are:

| T / K | Engine $a_{assoc}$ | FeOs−Engine | Clapeyron−Engine |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 298.15 | −2.599352552304062 | −8.88e-16 | −8.75e-14 |
| 323.15 | −2.111356600522939 | 0 | −9.50e-14 |

The $10^{-12}$ association-energy target is met. Total Z at 323.15 K has a separate Clapeyron $1.32\times10^{-12}$ miss. Pressure is negative at these falsifiers, so real $\ln\phi$ is unavailable; energy and derivatives remain meaningful EOS evaluations, not equilibrium states.

All three nontrivial coexistence intervals contain water feed 0.5 at both temperatures. Engine's water-rich/water-poor endpoints are 0.99935665/0.31959730 at 298.15 K and 0.99873812/0.37319377 at 323.15 K; corresponding water-rich **mole** fractions are 0.26539201 and 0.20271342. Comparator endpoint differences are much smaller than the distance to the common feed. No feed movement is needed. Feed closure is at most $1.11\times10^{-16}$. These declared two-liquid solutions do not establish global discovery or stability.

## Source precision and remaining strict misses

The DH diagnostic evaluates the analytic source function

$$
f(y)=\frac{\log(1+y)-y+y^2/2}{y^3},\qquad f(0)=1/3,
$$

its small-y series, Clapeyron's rational expression, and first/second derivatives at every actual solution/reference screening argument and on both sides of 1.5. Native Julia automatic differentiation propagates the signed source discrepancy into energy, Z and residual chemical potential. The 256/512-bit repeats and successive analytic-pressure-root refinements are retained. Corrections are outside timing; they do not replace returned library values.

Pressure correction is library-minus-analytic at one state. At the library root the displacement toward the analytic root is $\Delta\rho=+\delta P/P_{analytic,\rho}$. Solution, ionic-reference and pure-solvent corrections are applied independently before contracting coefficients. Observed refinement changes are numerical diagnostics, not rigorous accuracy bounds. FeOs dispersion/polar coefficient differences and dipole conversion are computed from the retained source coefficients; FeOs DH cancellation is not assigned Clapeyron's rational-approximation error model.

Maxima after the stated source corrections:

| Case | FeOs $|\Delta a^r|$ / $|\Delta Z|$ / $|\Delta\ln\phi|$ | Clapeyron $|\Delta a^r|$ / $|\Delta Z|$ / $|\Delta\ln\phi|$ |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | 8.52e-15 / 1.25e-14 / **1.43e-11** | 1.78e-15 / 1.19e-14 / **1.36e-11** |
| C2 | 3.07e-15 / 5.35e-15 / 1.05e-13 | 3.11e-15 / 3.46e-15 / 8.57e-14 |
| C3 | 1.00e-14 / 7.05e-14 / **1.68e-10** | 1.61e-14 / 6.69e-14 / **9.18e-11** |
| C4 | 8.73e-15 / 4.58e-14 / **3.93e-11** | 3.87e-13 / **1.32e-12** / **3.29e-10** |
| C5 | 7.69e-15 / 6.46e-15 / **6.48e-12** | 1.78e-15 / 1.40e-14 / 6.27e-13 |

Bold entries miss the unchanged absolute target ($10^{-12}$ neutral/dipolar, $10^{-11}$ C3). $\mu^r/(RT)$ is a localization diagnostic, not an additionally invented agreement target. For each log-fugacity row the retained decomposition uses

$$
\ln\phi_i=\mu_i^r/(RT)-\ln Z.
$$

For the same-density C3 FeOs contrast, the remaining $\ln\phi$ difference is about $-1.68\times10^{-10}$, while the chemical-potential remainder is only $1.68\times10^{-14}$: the logarithmic Z remainder dominates. This is an observed decomposition, not a residual-times-conditioning accuracy bound. In contrast, the C4 Clapeyron pentanol component in the 298.15 K water-rich liquid has chemical remainder $-3.0663\times10^{-10}$ and log-Z remainder $-2.1944\times10^{-11}$; blaming that whole miss on small Z would be incorrect.

The documented `AssocOptions(implicit_ad=true)` attempt has no effect on the C4 remainder. Raising evaluation precision to 256 bits also preserves it (chemical maximum $3.0653\times10^{-10}$). The source's compressed two-by-two association initializer uses a hardcoded $10^{-12}$ stopping threshold and returns before the general solver's tolerance/implicit-AD path. The 40-row retained diagnostic confirms a four-by-four native site matrix compressed to two-by-two. Tightening atol/rtol to 1e-30 also leaves the reported state quantities unchanged at each precision. This reproduces the source routing limitation, not merely an inference from the flag name. No library method is overwritten, and no corrected derivative is substituted into the benchmark.

For Engine C3, reduced residual alone does not guarantee relative pressure closure: $r=(P(\rho)-P_{target})/(\rho RT)$ and $|P(\rho)-P_{target}|/P_{target}=|r|/Z_{target}$, where $Z_{target}=P_{target}/(\rho RT)$. The owner-authorized revision retains both endpoint pressure records and uses the smaller $|P-P_{target}|$ endpoint for Newton and publication, choosing the upper endpoint on a tie. It preserves the residual and radius criteria, safeguarded step, quarter-radius witness and iteration budget. The anchor publishes the sole stable root from its existing local scan and composes the convergence counts. The original [historical anchor probe](results/density-closure-probe.csv) remains separately identified; the new replay has retained native traces and wheel identities.

The native C4 volume-reseed diagnostic reduces maximum relative pressure closure to $4.97\times10^{-11}$ and chemical equality to $4.53\times10^{-11}$, meeting the original $10^{-10}$ target on these two retained splits. It leaves the original compositions fixed and uses each library-returned volume as the starting guess. This demonstrates a bounded remedy for the volume-closure miss, not a new automatic flash solve, association-derivative correction or replacement timing result.

For Clapeyron C4, the bounded proposals are to qualify that documented native volume-reseed call as an explicitly different output workload, and to return the compressed association initializer's stopping/derivative precision to its upstream numerical owner. Those are prospective remedies, not authority to overwrite source or primary outputs. If the accountable lead accepts a narrower result, it must preserve every failed target and state the supported solved-value/energy scope explicitly. **Issue completion or scope amendment remains with that lead; this notebook does not silently redefine acceptance.**

## Provenance, reproducibility and limits

Engine values and gradients come from one non-editable wheel, SHA-256 `da56e55eab2dac8b75c2497da07e4895d838d82d2d78b305e4a30b81bfef3950`, using Engine numerical owners from merged main `efcb50fc`. FeOs is 0.10.1; Julia is 1.13.1; Clapeyron is 0.6.29. [summary.json](results/summary.json) records host, controls, identities and explicit missing diagnostics; [FeOs controls](inputs/feos-controls.md) and [Julia controls](inputs/julia-source-controls.md) give native source locators and defaults. `Project.toml`, `Manifest.toml` and the FeOs lock are analysis-local, not Engine dependencies.

The dispersion and dipole coefficient CSVs retain their executed CRLF bytes. Their input-directory `.gitattributes` disables line-ending normalization for these two files, preserving the committed bytes against the original `input_table_sha256` identities without changing coefficients or results.

Python declares inputs and compares/plots returned results. Engine EOS, equilibrium and gradients run natively in C++; comparator EOS and automatic differentiation run natively in Rust/Julia; source-error refinements and reference linear regression runs in Julia. FeOs activity contraction is an analysis-local Julia adapter, not an advertised FeOs native helper. No Python root solve, finite difference, activity equation or optimizer is introduced.

The [README](README.md) gives reproduction commands. Rendering reads this retained narrative and figure only; it does not run thermodynamics. Comparator caches stay available through delivered review and only task-owned caches may then be removed. Source locks/hashes, raw misses and diagnostic rows remain.

Claim limits: only the printed parameter packets, temperatures, compositions, declared phases, constant-permittivity/Born-off electrolyte selection and retained derivative coordinates are covered. The analysis neither adopts new parameters nor validates experimental thermodynamics, fits applications, establishes global stability, demonstrates Clapeyron parameter gradients, or extrapolates timings to other hosts. The unresolved strict closure/derivative findings prevent a blanket precision claim.
